description.value: A functional MRI study examined how sex, cocaine dependence, and individualized stress, drug/alcohol cue, and neutral-relaxing imagery conditions influence regional brain activation and craving.

value: we hypothesized that we would observe a three-way interaction of sex, diagnostic group, and cue condition with respect to corticostriatal-limbic activation.

We hypothesized that this three-way interaction would involve cocaine-dependent women showing greater corticostriatal activation to stress cues than comparison women and cocaine-dependent men showing greater activation to drug/alcohol cues than comparison men.

We also hypothesized that among cocaine-dependent women, subjective measures of stress-induced craving would correlate positively with stress cue condition-related corticostriatal-limbic activation and that among cocaine-dependent men, subjective measures of drug-induced craving would correlate positively with drug cue condition-related corticostriatal-limbic activation.
